newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks notch up new record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks notch up new record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks chalked up their fifth record close of the month on Wednesday, as investors who had kept on the sidelines earlier in the week were encouraged by renewed stability in the currency and bond markets.
"The main fundamental reason for the rally is less pressure from the forex and money markets," said Esteban Rojas, an equity analyst at the Arka brokerage.
The leading IPC share index rose 51.25 points, or 1.24 percent, to 4,194.44, surpassing its previous record of 4,160.85 points set on June 6.
In the broader market, gainers outpaced losers by 67 to 32 out of a total of 118 stocks traded, on heavy volume of 133.2 million shares.
Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes at 20.43 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, an increase of 113 basis points since last week.
Analysts said that on this occasion higher interest rates benefited stocks because they eased pressure on the Mexican peso and helped stabilise a volatile secondary money market.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 1.2 centavos firmer at 7.9640/7.9660 per dollar.
Overnight Cetes traded on the secondary market, meanwhile, plunged 210 basis points to close at 21.40 percent.
"Although we don't always follow Wall Street, it helped today," Rojas said, referring to the Dow Jones industrial average climb on Wednesday by 36.56 points to a record 7,575.83.
"Now we face a tough resistance at 4,200 points," he said.
"Every one was in the market today, locals and foreigners," a desk trader said. "But there was no overall or sectoral trend, many stocks climbed on invidual strength."

Among blue chips, Telmex led the rally, gaining 28 centavos (4 cents) to a new record close in peso terms of 18.92 pesos ($2.38). Its American Depository Receipts advanced 5/8 to 47-1/2 on the New York Stock Exchange as the Dow index rallied and an international brokerage raised the telecommunications company's earnings estimates.

Shares listed by Bancomer, one of Mexico's largest financial groups, weighed most on the market and were the most heavily traded of the day. Bancomer B shares ended down 10 centavos (1 cent) to 3.27 pesos (41 cents).

Dealers noted the stock had nonetheless recovered from a session low of 3.25 pesos (41 cents), despite the adverse effect of higher interest rates on hefty past-due loans held by the firm's banking division.
"Many felt Friday's close of 3.50 pesos (44 cents) was excessive, so they have been selling, but some are buying again now the secondary money market has sold down," a desk trader said.
Retailer Cifra and tortilla maker Maseca also posted notable gains. Maseca gained 38 centavos (5 cents) to 8.28 pesos ($1.04) on a change in government subsidies to tortillas, a Mexican staple.
Cifra gained 40 centavos (5 cents) to 13.72 pesos ($1.72) on what traders said was speculation over the settling price per share for a merger deal announced last week with Wal-Mart Stores Inc.
